props.title: Detective Conan: Jolly Roger in the Deep Azure

sections.content: Detective Conan: Jolly Roger in the Deep Azure stands as the 11th film in the Detective Conan franchise, delivering a maritime mystery that perfectly balances the series' signature deduction elements with high-stakes action. Like The Adventures of Tintin (2011) and Murder on the Orient Express (2017), it demonstrates how confined settings - in this case, a luxury cruise ship - can amplify tension in detective narratives. The film cleverly incorporates pirate mythology and modern technology, similar to how Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl (2003) revitalized maritime adventure for contemporary audiences.

sections.content: The film's underwater sequences and naval elements echo sophisticated maritime thrillers like The Abyss (1989) and Deep Blue Sea (1999), while maintaining the intricate mystery-solving that defines the Detective Conan series. The integration of historical pirate lore with modern criminal enterprises creates a compelling narrative layer, reminiscent of how National Treasure (2004) wove historical mysteries into contemporary adventures.

What sets this installment apart is its sophisticated handling of multiple plot threads - the primary murder mystery, the pirate treasure hunt, and the interpersonal dynamics among the passengers. This multi-layered approach recalls complex mystery films like Knives Out (2019) and Death on the Nile (2022), where the environment becomes as crucial to the story as the characters themselves. sections.content: The film represents a significant evolution in how anime handles maritime mysteries, setting a standard that influenced later works like One Piece Film: Strong World (2009) and Detective Conan: The Scarlet Bullet (2021). Its blend of traditional detective work with modern forensics and technology creates a unique viewing experience that bridges classic mystery conventions with contemporary storytelling techniques.
